html:
The Battle of Jahra was fought in October 1920 at the oasis of Jahra, west of Kuwait town, between Kuwaiti defenders and the Ikhwan, the zealous Bedouin warriors of Ibn Saud.

The Ikhwan, led by Faisal al-Dawish, attacked the village. The Kuwaitis under Sheikh Salim held out in the mud-walled Red Fort until the attackers withdrew. Kuwait town then built a new wall in a hurry, and British warships and planes showed they would defend it.

The battle saved Kuwait from being swallowed by the new Saudi state. Two years later Britain drew the borders in the Uqair Protocol, which gave much of Kuwait's claimed land to Ibn Saud. See also the Ikhwan colonies.
